citationText: 10. Technicolor's three-strip camera could not accommodate the CinemaScope lens. At the same time, Fox found Eastman Kodak negatives superior, providing release prints with “better color and definition” (according to Sponable). A 1957 memo explains Fox's switch to Eastman Color as follows: “CinemaScope imposed requirements of resolution and definition on the motion picture image which Technicolor at that lime seemed unable to meet” (letter from Skouras to Kay Harrison of French Technicolor, dated April 19, 1957). Fox was forced, however, to rely on Technicolor for the processing of some domestic and almost all foreign release prints due to the large demand for prints of The Robe and other early CinemaScope features, a demand which their own lab, Deluxe, was not yet equipped to meet. In a memo to Skouras and others (dated March 4, 1954), Zanuck himself faulted Technicolor's dye-transfer release prints for their low definition and softness.
